note: Pinned and dispatched. Paired on the same 498 questions and the same endpoint it beat the adopted arm by 4.84pp (p = 0.0160) while the four component readings summed to less than that gap, which is the whole argument for copying a pipeline instead of pricing its levers one at a time.
Pinned. Five agents, ten candidates drawn twice, unit tests generated and evaluated: the run needs an embedding model and a few hundred calls, so it is dispatched rather than run per push.

The README's roadmap lists the four withheld modules as future releases, and `ScaleSQL/modules` holds only the schema side, so the repository is the preprocessing half of an 81.67% test run. Running it produces a schema, not a system: the number it would make belongs to a hybrid and may not be plotted as theirs. Also the first leader in this queue whose gain is largely a 32B fine-tune plus vLLM, which this repository cannot host behind an API.

No release exists: the leaderboard row carries no repository and a GitHub search returns only community rebuilds. Four of the five mechanisms are already priced here (profile summary +3.6pp, three candidates, vote which lost 2.74pp to `shortest`, corrections bounded at 0.4pp); the open one is the linker, whose own ablation puts it at +1.8pp against +6.2pp for perfect linking. One community rebuild of the four-stage pipeline reports 95.6% mean column recall and 90.5% F1 in linking but 61.8% BIRD accuracy against the paper's 76.14-78.49 dev, which is what a rebuild of the published part buys when the unpublished part is the prompt text and the eight retrieved examples.
